articleBody:
Before starting demolition on your bathroom, going through a comprehensive checklist helps avoid unexpected delays, surprise plumbing adjustments, or water damage headaches down the road.

- [ ] Measure existing alcove width and depth — Ensures your new shower pan or custom base matches the existing wall envelope without requiring unexpected framing alterations.
- [ ] Verify subfloor condition around the tub base — Uncovers soft spots, past leaks, or rotting wood that must be addressed before installing new tile or mortar.
- [ ] Confirm drain pipe diameter and location — Determines if your plumbing lines need to be enlarged or shifted to meet local building codes for standalone showers.
- [ ] Determine curb preference versus curbless transition — Dictates whether your installer needs to recess subfloor joists to create a zero-barrier walk-in entry.
- [ ] Plan in-wall blocking for future grab bars — Secures solid structural framing points behind the wall substrate before tile installation so safety bars can be added safely anytime.
- [ ] Select shower control and valve heights — Adapts the rough-in plumbing to your household's height preferences and ensures handheld wands are easily reachable.
- [ ] Verify local permit requirements with Hillsborough County — Confirms whether building and plumbing permits are needed before work starts to maintain code compliance.
- [ ] Select moisture-resistant wall backing and waterproofing membranes — Protects interior framing against humidity and moisture intrusion in high-use Florida bathrooms.

How to use this checklist:
